github_issue.notes: The problem statement is grounded and verified: the two existing axes and AXIS_ABBREVIATION {'caller':'clr','target':'tgt'} exist in registry/rate_limiting/models.py:49, the floors rate_limit_user_floor_per_min/agent exist in registry/core/config.py:1530-1535, and the 403-without-marker-stays-403 mechanism is confirmed in docker/nginx_rev_proxy_http_and_https.conf @forbidden_error. All 15 acceptance criteria are testable (exact ids, status codes, metric name, header absence) and the out-of-scope list is explicit with reasons (fail-closed knob, control-plane, Redis, auto-quarantine). The largest deficiencies are minor: the user story promises denial "immediately" while propagation is bounded by the ~30s memberships cache TTL (never stated in the issue), and one AC attributes tool/skill rejection to _validate_enforceable when the model's entity-type allowlist would do it for caller_target. No unverifiable claim beyond issue numbers #295/#1504, which are at least consistent with in-repo references to issue 295.

lld.notes: This is the strongest artifact: every named file exists, and the cited line ranges are exactly right (limiter.py:116-156 _build_caller_gates, limiter.py:239-299 _enforce, models.py:153-155/197-199/226-243, auth_server/server.py:1409-1426), which I verified against the source. The load-bearing decisions are all made and correct: unconditional quarantine read outside the admin-skip block (the real limiter.py:218 'if not is_admin' guard), identity-keyed composite counter subject, validator exemption for limit-less markers with the existing limit_for_caller_type()-is-None filter as backstop, and headers() suppression matching the nginx rewrite keying on X-RateLimit-Throttled. Two soft spots keep it below exceptional: the claim that '@' cannot appear in usernames is asserted then walked back, and the constraint note that the machine-readable reason 'must live in the JSON detail of the parent response' is muddled since nginx's @forbidden_error discards the auth-server body entirely; the nginx templates path is also cited as docker/nginx/templates rather than docker/nginx_rev_proxy_*.conf. Rollback, fail-open rationale, TTL propagation, and cardinality discipline are all addressed concretely.

review.notes: The review does real work rather than role-play: Byte #2 catches a genuine defect I confirmed (check() skips the memberships read for admins at limiter.py:218, so a naive quarantine check inside that block would let admins bypass the kill switch), Cipher #1 honestly frames fail-open as a documented accepted risk rather than pretending it away, and Pixel #1's prefix-matching concern produces the exact-id isQuarantineMarker rule. The largest defect is Byte #1 being labeled critical on a false crash claim: the existing 'if limit is None: continue' in _build_caller_gates (limiter.py:138-139) already prevents the claimed TypeError, so the finding is belt-and-braces, not a blocker. Sage #2's '@'-separator analysis rambles and self-corrects mid-paragraph, and no reviewer examines the client's GET-then-PUT merge race or the route-layer test gap. Verdicts, resolutions, and a summary table tie findings to concrete LLD revisions.

testing.notes: The plan covers the right levels with real oracles: curl tests with exact definition/membership ids that match the route signatures (POST /api/rate-limits-enabled/{id}?enabled=, PUT membership id matching build_id()), CLI verbs that exist in the patch, five E2E scenarios including precedence-over-throttle and recovery, a strong backwards-compat section, and a rollback analysis whose inert-marker claim I verified against the old code's None-limit skip and malformed-doc skipping. Two concrete correctness errors: it invokes 'registry-cli' though the repo documents 'uv run python api/registry_management.py' and no such entrypoint exists in pyproject.toml, and E2E-2/UX expect the client-visible body {"error":"quarantined"} through the gateway, which is impossible because nginx's @forbidden_error returns a fixed body and discards the auth-server detail. It also promises extensions to tests/unit/api/test_rate_limit_routes.py and test_models.py that the submitted patch does not contain, leaving the new admin-API guards covered only by unexecuted manual procedures.

implementation.notes: The patch is real and fits the repository: I dry-ran git apply --check against the working tree for all 14 modified files successfully (the limiter.py hunks under --recount) and read every hunk against the actual source — context, symbols, and conventions match, including the cached-repository pattern, route guard functions, CLI dispatch dict, meters mcpgw_ naming, and test fakes mirroring tests/unit/rate_limiting/test_limiter.py under asyncio_mode=auto. The enforcement logic is correct end to end: quarantine pre-check before any gate, unconditional membership read binding admins, empty headers() so nginx leaves the 403 intact, None-limit marker guard, pairing guards, and idempotent best-effort seeding in the lifespan block at registry/main.py:780. The largest gaps are the absence of the route/model unit-test extensions the testing plan promises (reserved-name/marker/pairing guards have no automated coverage) and small defects: the LLD-promised asyncio.wait_for timeout around quarantine store reads is missing (try/except only), and rate_limit_errors_total is always labeled axis=caller even for target-side store errors. The summary is honest about deviations (client-side mirrored constants, UI panel folded into chips) and accurately reports what was not run.

verdict: A well-grounded, near-production-quality design and implementation whose largest material limitation is the client-facing quarantine oracle: nginx discards the auth-server body so error=quarantined never reaches callers through the gateway, and the new admin-API guards ship with no automated test coverage.
